PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Age: 14 years
Sex: Female
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Skin biopsy tissue section
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Anatomic Site: [redacted location]
Clinical History: Intradermal Spitz lesion with deep mitotic figures

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

NOTE: This report includes FISH studies only. No G-banded chromosome analysis was performed.

METHODOLOGY
FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using commercially available probes. Hybridization and washing were performed according to manufacturer's protocols. A minimum of 100 interphase nuclei were scored for each probe set.

Probes utilized:
- RREB1 (6p25)
- MYB (6q23)
- CCND1 (11q13)
- CEP6 (chromosome 6 centromere)

RESULTS
FISH analysis completed on skin biopsy specimen.

RREB1/MYB/CCND1/CEP6: No significant copy number alterations detected
- RREB1: 2 signals in 98% of cells
- MYB: 2 signals in 97% of cells
- CCND1: 2 signals in 99% of cells
- CEP6: 2 signals in 98% of cells

INTERPRETATION
The FISH analysis shows no evidence of copy number alterations in RREB1, MYB, or CCND1 genes. These findings do not support a diagnosis of melanoma. The absence of these alterations is consistent with a benign Spitz nevus, though does not definitively exclude an atypical Spitz tumor.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
The FISH results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathologic findings. The presence of deep mitotic figures noted in the clinical history warrants careful clinical follow-up despite negative FISH findings.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No additional genetic testing required at this time. Clinical follow-up as per dermatopathology recommendations.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
